sections.html:
Centennial is a home rule city in Arapahoe County, south of Denver. Interstate 25 roughly divides the city in half, and most business and entertainment centers are west of the highway.

The city covers about 29.9 square miles at an elevation of 5,722 feet. The landscape has many hills, gullies and ravines, with parks and trails such as the High Line Canal Trail and Dry Creek Dam. Arapahoe County, not the city, bills and collects your property tax, so the county's offices matter as much as city hall when you sell.

sections.h2: How did Centennial become a city?
sections.html:
Centennial is young. Voters approved incorporation on September 12, 2000, with 77 percent support, and the city was incorporated on February 7, 2001.

The area had more than 100,000 residents, which made it the largest incorporation in U.S. history at the time. The name reflects Colorado's 1876 admission as the 38th state, the centennial year of the Declaration of Independence. Voters approved home rule in 2008 by roughly a 2 to 1 margin.

sections.h2: How many people live in Centennial?
sections.html:
Centennial had 108,418 residents in the 2020 census, which made it the 11th most populous municipality in Colorado. A 2024 estimate put it at 108,853 and the Census Bureau estimate for July 1, 2025 is 108,658.

The median age is 37.2 years and the 2020 density was 3,648 people per square mile. The two estimates sit close to the 2020 count, which points to a settled city rather than a fast-growing one.

Centennial's employer list is led by large corporate and health care names. The city's 2023 annual financial report lists Comcast, UnitedHealthcare, Arrow Electronics, United Launch Alliance, CommonSpirit Health, Sierra Nevada Corporation, The Travelers Indemnity Company, RingCentral, Standard and Poor's, and MasTec Advanced Technologies.

Arrow Electronics is the largest company headquartered in Colorado. The National Cattlemen's Beef Association has its headquarters here, and an IKEA store opened on July 27, 2011. Dove Valley, an unincorporated area bordering the city, hosts the Denver Broncos' headquarters and training facilities.

sections.h2: What roads and airports serve Centennial?
sections.html:
Interstate 25 runs through Centennial and is the city's main corridor. Centennial Airport, formerly the Arapahoe County Airport, is adjacent to the city but sits on unincorporated county land, and it predates the city by more than 30 years.

If your house is near the airport or the interstate, mention that plainly to buyers. Noise is the sort of detail an inspector or neighbor will raise anyway.

Most of Centennial is served by Cherry Creek Public Schools, and the western portion is served by Littleton Public Schools. Private elementary and middle schools in the city include St. Thomas More Parish School, Highlands Baptist Academy, Shepherd of the Hills Christian School, Centennial Christian Academy and C.A.R.E. Middle School.

The district line runs through the city, so the district for your address depends on which side of it you live on.

sections.h2: What are Centennial's rules for replacing a roof?
sections.html:
In Centennial, a roof repair over 100 square feet is a major repair that needs a permit, while smaller repairs do not. The city's building division also says repairs that exceed 25 percent of the total roof area require a complete tear off and reroof.

  • Work must meet the 2021 International Residential Code.
  • A replacement removes all existing layers of roof covering to the deck.
  • Drip edge is required on all roof edges, and an ice barrier underlayment is required on all roofs.
  • Used or harvested materials are not allowed.
  • A mid-roof inspection is required for every reroof permit, and it may be done by photo.

Age and storm damage push owners toward roof work, and these rules affect what it costs and how long it takes. See the city's residential roof page. A buyer who purchases as-is takes on that work instead of you.

sections.h2: How does Arapahoe County handle property tax for a Centennial house?
sections.html:
The Arapahoe County Treasurer collects property tax for Centennial homes and distributes it to the county, school districts and other local governments. The treasurer's page says 2025 is a revaluation year, that a temporary state exemption used in 2023 and 2024 has expired, and that residential property uses two assessment rates, 6.25 percent for local government and 7.05 percent for schools.

  • Senior and military deferral applications are accepted January 1 through April 1.
  • Certificate of Taxes Due requests are handled for individuals and for title companies.
  • Excess foreclosure funds are handled by the Public Trustee.

For payment dates and questions, call the Treasurer's Office at 303-795-4550 or see the Arapahoe County Treasurer page. We did not confirm the exact due dates on that page, so check them there.

Centennial uses a council-manager form of government with eight council members. Home rule, approved by voters in 2008, lets the city set many of its own local rules.

The city was incorporated in part to block further annexations by Greenwood Village, and that history is one reason the city's boundaries and the county's unincorporated pockets, such as Dove Valley, sit side by side. Which jurisdiction covers your street decides who issues permits and enforces code, so confirm it before starting repairs.

sections.h2: What steps does a cash sale in Centennial follow?
sections.html:
A cash sale in Centennial moves through title and recording like any other sale, minus the lender. The steps are:

  1. You send the address and tell us about the house.
  2. We review it and make a written offer for the property as it stands.
  3. A title company confirms the Arapahoe County tax status and any liens.
  4. You choose a closing date, sign, and receive the agreed proceeds.

You can compare the offer with a listing, and you owe nothing if you decline.

sections.h2: What do Centennial sellers usually face?
sections.html:
Centennial sellers often have a well-located house that needs updating and a short window to sell. Typical situations include:

  • An inherited house that heirs live too far away to manage
  • A roof or systems that need work before a buyer's inspection
  • A move tied to an employer or to a divorce
  • A tenant in place who has to be dealt with

A cash sale replaces the lender and appraisal with a direct purchase and a closing date you can pick. You can still list the house instead if that fits better.

faqs.q: What county is Centennial, CO in?
faqs.a: Centennial is in Arapahoe County, which collects the property tax.
Voters approved incorporation on September 12, 2000, and the city was incorporated on February 7, 2001.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to replace a roof in Centennial?
faqs.a: Yes for a major repair or replacement. Repairs under 100 square feet are small and need no permit, and larger work requires one.

faqs.q: Which school district is Centennial in?
faqs.a: Most of the city is in Cherry Creek Public Schools, and the western portion is in Littleton Public Schools.

faqs.q: Who handles the Certificate of Taxes Due in Arapahoe County?
faqs.a: The Arapahoe County Treasurer handles those requests for individuals and for title companies. Your title company will normally order it for a sale.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Centennial house with an old roof?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer purchases as-is, so you do not need to replace the roof before closing. Ask for the offer in writing.
